svg.title: A shorted quarter-wave line looks like an open circuit
svg.desc: Left: a line a quarter wavelength long ending in a short. Along it the voltage envelope rises from zero at the short to a maximum at the input, while the current falls from a maximum at the short to zero at the input, so the input looks open. Right: on the Smith chart the short sits at the left edge and a quarter wave of line rotates it half a turn clockwise, through the inductive top half, to the open at the right edge.
svg.text: λ/4 of line turns a short into an open
λ/4 toward the generator = half a turn
Lossless shorted line: |V| ∝ |sin βd|, |I| ∝ |cos βd| at distance d from the short. Zin = jZ₀ tan βℓ → ∞ at ℓ = λ/4.
